artworks.title: Thyestes and Aerope
artworks.description: Nosadella paints Aerope with Thyestes — Atreus' Cretan wife whose adultery and the stolen golden lamb token open the Mycenaean feud. She is the queen whose betrayal precedes the feast that made the house proverbial.

artworks.title: Les Pélopides (Voltaire)
artworks.description: Moreau's illustration for Voltaire's Pelopid tragedy keeps Aerope's generation on the Enlightenment stage — the adulterous queen still written into the curse that runs from Tantalus to Agamemnon.

artworks.title: The Feast of Atreus and Thyestes
artworks.artist: Václav Jindřich Nosecký and Michael Wenzel Halbax
artworks.description: The Zákupy banquet mural is the sequel Aerope's betrayal helped ignite: Atreus serving Thyestes his own children — the horror that follows the stolen wife and the golden fleece of Mycenae.

popCulture.title: Thyestes
popCulture.creator: Seneca the Younger
popCulture.description: Seneca's revenge play inherits Aerope as the wife Atreus punishes through the feast — her adultery the first wound in the Pelopid cycle the stage never forgot.

popCulture.title: Aerope
popCulture.description: Cretan daughter of Catreus, wife of Atreus, mother of Agamemnon and Menelaus — lover of Thyestes in the quarrel over the Mycenaean throne.
